title: Shuffle a seating line
prompt:
head is a line of guests L0, L1, ..., Ln stored as a singly linked list; relink it in place into the order L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, L2, ... and return the head.

- Each node is an object with val (an integer) and next (the next node or null; None in Python). In Python, nodes are dicts: node["val"], node["next"].
- The list has 0 to 300 nodes; an empty list is null (None).
- Relink the existing nodes with O(1) extra space (no arrays of nodes).
hints: The result alternates between the front half in order and the back half in reverse. Can you get those two lists separately?
Find the middle with slow/fast pointers, cut the list there, and reverse the second half.
Merge by alternating: take one node from the first half, then one from the reversed second half. The first half has the extra node when the length is odd.

solution.js:
function interleaveHalves(head) {
  if (head === null || head.next === null) return head
  let slow = head
  let fast = head
  while (fast.next !== null && fast.next.next !== null) {
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
  }
  let second = slow.next
  slow.next = null
  let prev = null
  while (second !== null) {
    const next = second.next
    second.next = prev
    prev = second
    second = next
  }
  let first = head
  second = prev
  while (second !== null) {
    const firstNext = first.next
    const secondNext = second.next
    first.next = second
    second.next = firstNext
    first = firstNext
    second = secondNext
  }
  return head
}
solution.py:
def interleave_halves(head):
    if head is None or head["next"] is None:
        return head
    slow = fast = head
    while fast["next"] is not None and fast["next"]["next"] is not None:
        slow = slow["next"]
        fast = fast["next"]["next"]
    second = slow["next"]
    slow["next"] = None
    prev = None
    while second is not None:
        nxt = second["next"]
        second["next"] = prev
        prev, second = second, nxt
    first, second = head, prev
    while second is not None:
        first_next, second_next = first["next"], second["next"]
        first["next"] = second
        second["next"] = first_next
        first, second = first_next, second_next
    return head
solution.explanation: The target order zips the first half with the reversed second half. Slow/fast pointers find the end of the first half (the larger half for odd lengths), an in-place reversal prepares the second half, and alternating links merge them without extra memory.

complexity.notes: Three linear passes: find middle, reverse, merge.

followUps: Undo the shuffle: restore the original order from L0, Ln, L1, Ln-1, ...
Do it with an O(n) stack of nodes instead. When might that be acceptable?
